title: Representing the universal rank clause without canonical map conditions
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume that for every $g:T\to S$ the tensor-pullback/pushforward adjunction unit at $\mathcal O_T$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] for $p_g:X\times_S T\to T$ is an isomorphism. Let $E$ be finite locally free [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. There exist a scheme $W$ and an immersion $j:W\to S$, locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact, such that for every $g:T\to S$, $g$ factors through $j$ if and only if $R(f,E,g)$ [def-sc-picard-universal-rank-match]. No canonical base-change-map invertibility is part of the representing condition.

proof.text: Apply the unit hypothesis to residue-field base changes. Global functions on each fibre form its residue field, so the fibre is nonempty and connected. The normalized-fibre theorem supplies the connectedness implication after identifying the unit map on sections. The open-and-closed rank loci of E have open images by flat finite presentation and closed images by properness. Fibre connectedness makes these images disjoint; nonemptiness makes them cover S. This is the open-and-closed rank decomposition.

On each rank-r component, E and its dual are finitely presented and relatively flat. Their derived direct images are perfect with arbitrary base change. Vanishing of all negative cohomology after every base change gives local finite-free models of Tor amplitude [0,b]. Degree-zero derived direct image is the ordinary pushforward.

Apply the universal lowest-cohomology rank-r locus to each complex and take the fibre product. Its universal property gives precisely the two universal ordinary direct-image rank-r conditions. Refine neighbourhoods to compare them with the constant rank-r pullback of E. Glue across amplitude charts using the unique representing identifications, then take the disjoint union across rank components. Immersion and local finite presentation are local on the target. A quasi-compact target open meets finitely many components, on each of which the rank loci are quasi-compact; thus the union is quasi-compact. The rank-zero model has zero first term; empty tests are vacuous.

theorem exists_picardUniversalRankMatchLocus {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hO : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S),
      IsIso ((Classical.choose
        (Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (pullback.snd f g))).unit.app
          (SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf)))
    (E : X.Modules) [E.IsFiniteLocallyFree] :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : W ⟶ S),
      IsImmersion j ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation j ∧ QuasiCompact j ∧
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S),
        (∃ h : T ⟶ W, h ≫ j = g) ↔ PicardUniversalRankMatch f E g
